# Lessons — cross-module findings with evidence

Only things backed by evidence go here. A method that works in one module stays in that module's
file until it works in a second one.

## L1. AI-generated course material is right where it copies, wrong where it embellishes (2026-11-17)

**Evidence:** audit of `modules/EEEE4138_aerial_robotics/chapters/` (generated by another AI tool,
"74/74 tests passed").
- `topic_5_flight_control.md:595`: "Worked Example 3 (Tutorial 5 Q2)". Every number differs from the
  real Q2, so every answer differs. The test script cites a third, different set of numbers under the
  same label.
- `topic_5_flight_control.md:584`: "hangs 5 cm *above* the target". The official T4 solution says
  **below** (NED, z down). The number was right; the interpretation was wrong.
- Invented specifics: "gimbal lock at |θ| ≥ 85°" (slides: ±90°), "k_i ≤ k_max/5 ⇒ ζ > 0.6".
- Its tests only checked structure (files exist, LaTeX balanced, sections present).
- Correct parts: rotation conventions, T1 Q6, the T2 Q1–3 / T4 Q3 / T5 Q4 statements, θ_d = −u_x/g,
  k_d > τ_m k_p. These were copied from the source.

**So:** focus verification on anything labelled as a source, anything re-parameterised, and every
sentence with a direction word. This is the basis of the fixed rules in SKILL.md.

## L2. Long, complete AI chapters don't help this student (2026-11-17)

**Evidence:** the same aerial material: 600–1000-line chapters, "API contract" tables for Euler
angles, widgets with up to 15 sliders and nothing asking for a prediction. The student found the
format to be the problem they started with (walls of text), and doesn't trust it.

**So:** default to small, student-driven steps (SKILL.md "Roles"). Build bigger material only when a
module's log shows it's needed. (visualisations, sliders etc are useful tools as well)
